name: Sierra
tagline: Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor's premium enterprise AI agent platform, valued at $15.8B in its May 2026 Series E — genuinely sophisticated architecture and real Fortune-50 traction, undercut by unusually thin public documentation of even basic CRM integrations for a company at this scale.
tldr: Sierra was founded in San Francisco in 2023 by Bret Taylor (former Salesforce co-CEO, OpenAI board chair) and Clay Bavor (former longtime Google executive), and has raised at an extraordinary pace — a $110M Series A, $175M Series B/C ($4.5B valuation), $350M Series D ($10B valuation), and a $950M Series E in May 2026 that pushed its valuation to $15.8B, one of the highest in this entire product category.

Reported ARR grew from roughly $100M (November 2025) to roughly $150M (February 2026) per TechCrunch, and the company counts over 40% of the Fortune 50 as customers, with named clients including SiriusXM, ADT, Wayfair, Nordstrom, Chime, SoFi, CarMax, and Redfin.

Its 'Agent OS' architecture composes agents from separate capabilities — retrieval, classification, tools, policies, tone — rather than one monolithic model, with dedicated supervisor agents that monitor and correct live conversations in real time, a genuinely sophisticated approach to guardrails.

A real, notable gap for a company at this scale and valuation: we found no named CRM, helpdesk, or CMS/ecommerce integrations documented anywhere on Sierra's own site — only generic language about connecting to 'your CRM, inventory, and other key systems' — and no public integrations marketplace exists at all, meaning Sierra appears to build bespoke, sales-engineering-led connections per customer rather than offering a self-serve integration catalog.

Pricing follows a genuinely interesting outcome-based model — Sierra is paid only when its agent resolves a case without human intervention, with escalated cases costing nothing — but there's no public pricing page, and industry analysts specifically criticize how 'resolution' gets defined as effectively a 'black box until the contract is signed.'

Independent review data is thin and partly unreachable (Trustpilot shows zero reviews on an unclaimed profile; G2 shows only 15-17 reviews with a rating that varies 4.1-4.3 across secondary sources), and Sierra's extremely high valuation for a company barely three years old has drawn genuine, publicly documented skepticism — though we found no evidence of billing fraud, account lockouts, or hostile support in any source reviewed.

faq.question: How is Sierra funded, and why is its valuation so high?
faq.answer: Sierra has raised at an extraordinary pace for a company founded in 2023 — reaching a $15.8B valuation in its May 2026 Series E ($950M, led by Tiger Global and GV). This scale, for a company barely three years old, has drawn genuine, publicly documented skepticism (including a Blind forum thread literally titled 'Is Sierra AI a scam?'), though the skepticism centers on organizational structure and pricing philosophy rather than any allegation of fraud, and Sierra's reported $150M ARR and Fortune-50-heavy customer base are offered by supporters as justification.

faq.question: Does Sierra integrate with Salesforce, Zendesk, or HubSpot?
faq.answer: This is genuinely unclear, and worth flagging directly given Sierra's scale and valuation. We found no named CRM or helpdesk vendors documented anywhere on Sierra's own site — only generic language about connecting to 'your CRM, inventory, and other key systems.' No public integrations marketplace or catalog exists at all, which suggests Sierra builds bespoke, sales-engineering-led connections per customer rather than offering a self-serve integration list most competitors publish.

faq.question: Does Sierra integrate with Shopify or other ecommerce platforms?
faq.answer: Not confirmed. Sierra's own retail industry page uses only generic integration language, with no named ecommerce or CMS platforms. Third-party blogs claim Shopify and WooCommerce connectivity, but we could not locate any primary Sierra announcement, documentation, or case study confirming this — treat these claims as unverified rather than fact.

faq.question: How does Sierra's pricing actually work?
faq.answer: Sierra uses outcome-based, per-resolution pricing — it's paid a pre-negotiated rate only when its agent fully resolves a case without human intervention, and cases escalated to a human cost nothing. This is a genuinely interesting, aligned-incentive model, confirmed directly by Bret Taylor in a public interview. However, there's no public pricing page, and industry analysts specifically criticize how 'resolution' gets defined in practice as effectively unclear until a contract is signed — a real transparency concern worth pushing on during any sales process.

faq.question: Can I get self-serve access to Sierra's API or developer documentation?
faq.answer: Not in the way most developer tools offer it. Sierra describes a 'modern developer experience' for building agents through its Agent SDK, but we could not locate a public API reference, webhook documentation, or developer portal. Extensibility appears to be delivered through Sierra's own forward-deployed engineering process rather than something you can sign up for and read documentation on independently.

faq.question: What do independent reviews say about Sierra?
faq.answer: The available data is thin. G2 shows only 15-17 reviews with a rating reported as either 4.1 or 4.3 depending on the source, and Trustpilot shows zero reviews on an unclaimed profile. Reported positive themes include ease of use and strong implementation support; negative themes include a steep learning curve, pricing opacity, limited self-service configuration, and voice latency from routing through multiple models for accuracy checks. We found no evidence of billing fraud, account lockouts, or hostile support in any source reviewed.

pricingBreakdown: Sierra's outcome-based pricing model is genuinely interesting and confirmed directly by co-founder Bret Taylor in a public interview: the company is paid a pre-negotiated rate only when its agent fully resolves a case without human intervention, and cases that get escalated to a human cost nothing — an aligned-incentive structure Taylor has explicitly compared to the shift from impression-based to click-based ad pricing. That said, there is no public pricing page, and third-party estimates (unverified against any Sierra-published figure) suggest roughly $1.50 per resolved interaction, setup fees in the $50,000-$200,000 range, and year-one all-in contracts commonly cited between $150,000 and $350,000-plus. The most important thing to know before entering a sales conversation: industry analysts specifically criticize how 'resolution' gets defined in practice as effectively unclear until a contract is signed, and the pricing model carries a real structural quirk — as the agent gets better at resolving cases without escalation, your bill can actually go up. Push for precise, contractual definitions of what counts as a billable resolution before committing.

capabilities.note: The 'Agent OS' approach — composing agents from separate capabilities (retrieval, classification, tools, policies, tone) with dedicated supervisor agents monitoring live conversations in real time — represents a real, thoughtfully engineered approach to reliability, distinct from a single monolithic model handling everything.

Over 40% of the Fortune 50 as customers, with named clients spanning SiriusXM, ADT, Wayfair, Nordstrom, Chime, SoFi, and CarMax, backed by reported ARR growth from roughly $100M to $150M in a few months — this is genuine, verifiable enterprise credibility, not just funding-round hype.

Worth stating plainly: for a company valued at $15.8B, we found it genuinely notable that no named CRM, helpdesk, or ecommerce/CMS integration is documented anywhere on Sierra's own site, and no public integrations marketplace exists at all. Every other enterprise-tier competitor we've researched in this category publishes at least a substantial CRM integration list — Sierra's complete reliance on bespoke, sales-engineering-led connections is a real difference worth factoring into any evaluation.

A $15.8B valuation for a company founded in 2023 has drawn genuine public skepticism, including a Blind forum thread literally asking 'Is Sierra AI a scam?' — though the skepticism centers on organizational structure and pricing philosophy questions, not fraud allegations, and we found no evidence of the more serious complaint patterns (billing fraud, lockouts, hostile support) that would justify real alarm.

verdict: Sierra's rapid ascent — from a 2023 founding to a $15.8B valuation in under three years, backed by Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor's pedigree and real Fortune-50 enterprise traction — reflects genuine investor and customer conviction, and the underlying architecture backs it up: 'Agent OS' composing agents from separate, purpose-built capabilities with dedicated supervisor agents monitoring live conversations is a thoughtfully engineered approach to reliability, not just marketing language. Reported ARR growth from roughly $100M to $150M in a few months, alongside named enterprise customers like Wayfair, Nordstrom, and SoFi, is real, verifiable traction. But we want to be direct about a gap that genuinely surprised us given the company's scale and valuation: we could not find a single named CRM, helpdesk, or ecommerce/CMS integration documented anywhere on Sierra's own site, and no public integrations marketplace exists at all — every other enterprise-tier competitor we've researched in this category publishes at least a substantial integration list, and Sierra's apparent reliance on entirely bespoke, sales-engineering-led connections is a meaningfully different (and less transparent) approach. The same theme extends to pricing and developer access: Sierra's outcome-based pricing model is a genuinely interesting, aligned-incentive innovation, but there's no public pricing page, and industry analysts specifically describe the definition of a billable 'resolution' as unclear until a contract is signed — and there's no public API documentation either, with extensibility delivered entirely through Sierra's own forward-deployed engineering rather than self-serve developer access. None of this points to fraud or misconduct — we found no evidence of billing fraud, lockouts, or hostile support anywhere — but it does mean Sierra asks for a higher degree of trust and negotiation upfront than most competitors in this category, consistent with its premium, high-touch enterprise positioning. If you're a large, well-resourced enterprise comfortable with a custom sales process and negotiating precise contractual terms, Sierra's architecture and traction are genuinely credible; if you want to evaluate integration depth or pricing transparency before committing significant sales-cycle time, that information simply isn't publicly available the way it is for other tools in this category.
